eventContext: Barrinha bot as a governed exception to the general anti-bot policy in Canal #barra
publicDescription: The archive records, based on BarMan's recollection, that bots were generally prohibited in Canal #barra. The Barrinha bot was treated as an exception because it was developed by Brumarx, an early Canal #barra participant, and because BarMan had access to edit the bot's periodic messages. This places Barrinha under a governance and editorial-control exception rather than treating it as an unrestricted automation layer.

claims.claim: Bots were generally prohibited in Canal #barra.
Barrinha was an exception to the general anti-bot policy.
Barrinha was developed by Brumarx, identified by the archive as an early Canal #barra participant.
BarMan had access to edit Barrinha's periodic messages, creating a form of editorial oversight over the bot's channel output.
Barrinha's messages could appear during live conversations and be mistaken by uninformed users for a human female participant, sometimes leading users to send private messages to the bot.

methodologyAlignment.supportsInterpretation: Canal #barra's automation policy was governance-sensitive: bots were not generally allowed, while Barrinha functioned as a trusted and editorially supervised exception.
